scope.objective: Support and delimit the preregistered repeated finite-population video-subsampling estimator and rank-fidelity diagnostics.

sources.title: Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife
supports: Resampling can approximate the sampling distribution of a prespecified statistic from observed data.
The bootstrap is a general resampling framework rather than a guarantee for every statistic or sampling design.
does_not_support: Calling the preregistered without-replacement video draws an ordinary Efron bootstrap.
Finite-sample validity for k in {3,5,8,12}, the nonlinear graph score, or the project acceptance thresholds.

sources.title: Large Sample Confidence Regions Based on Subsamples under Minimal Assumptions
supports: A statistic recomputed over subsamples can be used to approximate a sampling distribution.
Subsampling and the ordinary bootstrap are distinct resampling constructions.
does_not_support: Unqualified confidence-interval coverage for a fixed 36-video finite census or for this unstudentized nonlinear score.
The exact 10,000-draw Monte Carlo count or the width threshold 0.005.

sources.title: Asymptotic Normality and the Bootstrap in Stratified Sampling
supports: Bootstrap behavior under stratified sampling requires design-specific theory rather than automatic transfer from iid resampling.
Stratified resampling has an established asymptotic literature.
does_not_support: Equivalence between the paper's asymptotic setting and fixed small-k video sampling.
The residual-derived strata, nonlinear score reconstruction, or fidelity gate used here.

sources.title: A Generalization of Sampling Without Replacement from a Finite Universe
sources.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
sources.publisher: Taylor & Francis for the American Statistical Association
supports: Finite-population totals can be expanded under sampling without replacement using inverse inclusion probabilities.
For simple random sampling, inclusion probability k/N gives weight N/k; within stratum h, inclusion probability n_h/N_h gives weight N_h/n_h.
does_not_support: Unbiasedness of the final nonlinear ratio/Jaccard score after weighted sufficient statistics are plugged into the score.
A claim that candidate deltas share independent sampling errors.

sources.title: On the Two Different Aspects of the Representative Method: The Method of Stratified Sampling and the Method of Purposive Selection
sources.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society
sources.publisher: Wiley for the Royal Statistical Society
supports: Probability sampling within predefined strata is a principled way to represent heterogeneous finite populations.
Stratum allocation and stratum-specific expansion belong to the sampling design and must be accounted for in estimation.
does_not_support: That residual top-ten or family-by-residual are optimal strata for this benchmark.
That proportional largest-remainder allocation is Neyman optimal allocation; the preregistration uses proportional allocation, not variance-optimal allocation.

sources.title: The Proof and Measurement of Association between Two Things
supports: Rank correlation assesses preservation of ordinal association rather than equality on the original score scale.
Spearman rho is appropriate as a rank-fidelity diagnostic across candidates.
does_not_support: Median aggregation over draws, average-rank tie handling, sign agreement, or any promotion decision.

residual_top10.sampling_design: stratified random sampling without replacement with proportional largest-remainder allocation

family_residual.sampling_design: stratified random sampling without replacement on Cartesian family-by-residual strata

repeated_draw_distribution.interpretation: Monte Carlo approximation to the finite-population sampling-design distribution over eligible video subsets, not an ordinary iid bootstrap confidence distribution.

rank_fidelity.interpretation: Spearman rank association between candidate deltas on a draw and banked full deltas.

transfer_limits: The cited survey-sampling papers concern estimation of finite-population quantities, especially additive totals or means. Here those ideas transfer only to expansion of additive per-video sufficient statistics.
The official graph score is a nonlinear function of expanded totals. Inverse-probability expansion does not imply an unbiased score or unbiased delta after the nonlinear transformation.

The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles summarize the empirical design distribution of the subsample estimator over the authenticated finite video universe. They should not be advertised as a 95% confidence interval for an unknown superpopulation parameter.
The candidate vector is small and all candidates are evaluated on the same selected videos, so candidate errors and draw-level fidelity metrics are dependent.

Asymptotic bootstrap and subsampling results do not guarantee accuracy at k=3, 5, 8, or 12, nor for N approximately 36. Fidelity must therefore be established empirically against the banked full results.
Residual-based stratification is benchmark-specific. The literature supports accounting for a frozen stratified design, not the predictive sufficiency or optimality of these particular strata.

Spearman rho measures ordinal agreement only. Sign agreement and the maximum candidate interval width are needed project-specific complements; their thresholds are preregistered decisions, not literature-derived constants.
No source supports using a video subsample for promotion. The contract, if one is frozen, remains screening-only and every promotion still requires the full 44b6 gate.
